q01.key_idea: Every rope has 2 ends, so count the ends and share them out 2 by 2.
steps: Look for the rope ends. Each end has a black dot.
There are 6 dots: 2 on the left, 3 on the top right, and 1 at the bottom.
No rope is a closed ring, so every rope has exactly 2 ends.
6 ends make 3 pairs: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. So there are 3 ropes.

choice_feedback.A: 2 ropes would have only 4 ends, but there are 6 ends.
choice_feedback.C: 4 ropes would have 8 ends, but there are only 6 ends.
choice_feedback.D: 5 ropes would have 10 ends, but there are only 6 ends.
choice_feedback.E: 6 is the number of rope ends. Each rope has 2 ends.

q02.key_idea: Add the animals that live in the cave and the animals that visit.
steps: Animals that live in the cave: 1 starfish + 2 seahorses + 3 turtles = 6.
Visitors: 3 starfish + 4 turtles + 5 seahorses = 12.
All together: 6 + 12 = 18 animals.

choice_feedback.A: 6 is only the animals that live in the cave. The visitors are missing.
choice_feedback.B: Count every animal: 6 live there and 12 visit.
choice_feedback.C: 12 is only the visitors. The 6 animals that live there are missing.
choice_feedback.D: Count again: 6 animals live there and 12 visit, so there are more than 15.

q03.key_idea: Walk from O through the gaps in the walls and see where you can get to.
steps: From O, step out through a gap in the small wall around it.
Walk to the gap at the top of the next wall and go through it.
Turn left and walk around to the gap on the upper left of the next wall. Go through it into the outside ring.
Walk to the right along the outside ring up to the top. There you find C.

choice_feedback.A: A wall stands right next to the upper left gap, so you cannot walk down the outside ring to A.
choice_feedback.B: B is joined only to the part where E is, and that part is walled off from O.
choice_feedback.D: D is in a small room with walls all around it.
choice_feedback.E: E is close to O, but a wall stands between them.

q04.key_idea: Do not forget Robert himself. He is a boy too.
steps: 10 friends come and 6 of them are girls.
So 10 - 6 = 4 friends are boys.
Robert is also at the party, and he is a boy: 4 + 1 = 5 boys.

choice_feedback.A: 4 counts only the boy friends. Robert is a boy too.
choice_feedback.C: 6 is the number of girls, not boys.
choice_feedback.D: There are 4 boy friends plus Robert. That makes 5, not 7.
choice_feedback.E: There are 4 boy friends plus Robert. That makes 5, not 8.

q05.key_idea: When you count from one number to another, count both the first and the last house.
steps: From 15 to 47 there are 47 - 15 = 32 steps.
But house 15 gets a flyer too, so add 1 more.
32 + 1 = 33 houses.

choice_feedback.A: This leaves out 2 of the houses.

q06.key_idea: Count every cube, also the hidden ones that hold up the cubes on top.
steps: A cube that sits up high needs a cube under it, even if we cannot see it.
In A, the tall tower at the back has 3 cubes. The tower in front of it has 2 cubes.
In front of those towers there are 2 more cubes in a row. On the right side there are 3 more cubes.
3 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 10. That uses all 10 dice.

choice_feedback.B: B needs 12 cubes when you count the hidden ones under the towers.
choice_feedback.C: C has two towers of 3, 1 cube between them, 2 in front and 2 at the back: 11 cubes.
choice_feedback.D: D has a tower of 5 and 6 cubes around its bottom: 11 cubes.
choice_feedback.E: E has a tower of 3 and 8 more flat cubes around it: 11 cubes.

q07.key_idea: Eggs next to each other or one above the other touch, so each column can hold only 1 brown egg.
steps: The box has 2 rows with 3 eggs in each row, so there are 3 columns.
The 2 eggs in the same column touch, so each column can have at most 1 brown egg.
Put brown eggs top left, bottom middle, top right. They only meet corner to corner, so they do not touch.
That is 3 brown eggs, and 4 is not possible with only 3 columns.

choice_feedback.A: You can fit more: one brown egg in each column works.
choice_feedback.B: You can fit one more: one brown egg in each of the 3 columns.
choice_feedback.D: With 4 brown eggs, 2 of them would be in the same column and touch.
choice_feedback.E: With 5 brown eggs, many of them would touch each other.

q08.key_idea: Take away the cat's legs first, then share the rest in 2s.
steps: The cat has 4 legs. 20 - 4 = 16 legs are left.
Each chicken has 2 legs.
16 legs is 8 pairs of legs, so there are 8 chickens.

choice_feedback.A: 11 chickens would have 22 legs, even without the cat.
choice_feedback.B: 9 chickens have 18 legs. With the cat's 4 legs that is 22, not 20.
choice_feedback.D: 6 chickens have 12 legs. With the cat's 4 legs that is only 16.
choice_feedback.E: 4 chickens have 8 legs. With the cat's 4 legs that is only 12.

q09.key_idea: Each room with the light on has 2 bright windows.
steps: 18 windows are bright, and each lit room has 2 of them.
18 windows are 9 pairs, so the light was on in 9 rooms.
The house has 12 rooms: 12 - 9 = 3 rooms had the light off.

choice_feedback.A: If only 2 rooms were dark, 10 rooms would be lit with 20 bright windows.
choice_feedback.C: If 4 rooms were dark, 8 rooms would be lit with only 16 bright windows.
choice_feedback.D: If 6 rooms were dark, 6 rooms would be lit with only 12 bright windows.
choice_feedback.E: 9 is the number of rooms with the light on, not off.

q10.key_idea: In 4 years each of the two boys gets 4 years older.
steps: Now Paul and Josef are 12 years old together.
In 4 years Paul is 4 years older, and Josef is 4 years older too.

choice_feedback.A: 16 adds the 4 years only once. Both boys get older.
choice_feedback.B: Each boy gets 4 years older, so add 4 + 4 = 8 years.
choice_feedback.C: Each boy gets 4 years older, so add 4 + 4 = 8 years.
choice_feedback.D: Each boy gets 4 years older, so add 4 + 4 = 8 years.

q11.key_idea: Walk the road like Gerda and turn with her. Only write a letter when it is on her right hand side.
steps: From point 1 she walks up. The K is on her right.
She turns left and walks along the top. The A is inside, on her left. Then she walks down the left side, and the N is on her right.
She walks along the bottom. The G is inside, on her left. Then she walks up, and the A is on her right.
She walks along the small top part. The O there is on her left. Then she walks down to point 2, and the other O is on her right.
The letters on her right are K, N, A, O. That spells KNAO.

choice_feedback.B: The G is on her left side, not her right.
choice_feedback.C: The R is on her left side, and the A and O are missing.
choice_feedback.D: She sees the K first. The A at the top and the G are on her left.
choice_feedback.E: The N on the left side of the road is on her right, so it belongs in the word.

q12.key_idea: Try to cover each shape with pieces. Start with a square that has only one neighbour.
steps: Each piece is 3 squares in a row with 1 square sticking out of the middle.
In D, the top square only touches the square below it. So one piece must be the column of 3 on the left with its bump to the right.
The 4 squares left over make a zigzag step shape. That is not the piece shape.
So D cannot be made. Every other shape can be split into pieces.

choice_feedback.A: A can be made from 2 pieces, one with its bump up and one with its bump down.
choice_feedback.B: B can be made from 2 pieces: the left column with a bump, and the bottom right row with a bump up.
choice_feedback.C: C can be made from 2 pieces: the top row with a bump down, and the bottom row with a bump up.
choice_feedback.E: The big square can be made from 4 pieces, one along each side.

q13.key_idea: Look at which way each beak points, then count the sparrows on that side.
steps: From left to right, the beaks point: right, left, right, left, right.
Sparrow 1 looks right and sees 4. Sparrow 2 looks left and sees 1. Sparrow 3 looks right and sees 2.
Sparrow 4 looks left and sees 3. Sparrow 5 looks right and sees 0.

choice_feedback.E: Check which way each beak points. The last sparrow sees nobody.

q14.key_idea: For each ladybird, find the difference and the total of its spots, then find the flower that matches.
steps: Ladybirds, top wing and bottom wing: 5 and 2, 4 and 2, 4 and 3, 5 and 3, 6 and 1.
Their difference and total: 5 - 2 = 3 and 7; 4 - 2 = 2 and 6; 4 - 3 = 1 and 7; 5 - 3 = 2 and 8; 6 - 1 = 5 and 7.
Flowers, leaves and petals: A has 5 and 7, B has 1 and 7, C has 2 and 8, D has 3 and 7, E has 2 and 7.
A gets 6 and 1. B gets 4 and 3. C gets 5 and 3. D gets 5 and 2.
E needs a difference of 2 and a total of 7. No ladybird has that.

choice_feedback.A: The ladybird with 6 and 1 spots fits: 6 - 1 = 5 leaves and 6 + 1 = 7 petals.
choice_feedback.B: The ladybird with 4 and 3 spots fits: 4 - 3 = 1 leaf and 4 + 3 = 7 petals.
choice_feedback.C: The ladybird with 5 and 3 spots fits: 5 - 3 = 2 leaves and 5 + 3 = 8 petals.
choice_feedback.D: The ladybird with 5 and 2 spots fits: 5 - 2 = 3 leaves and 5 + 2 = 7 petals.

q15.key_idea: A side cannot be opposite a side it touches. Find the only side that never touches it.
steps: The side with the small square inside a square is in both pictures.
In the first cube it touches the side with a line and the side with a small diamond.
In the second cube it touches the side with 4 boxes and the side with the X.
It touches 4 sides. The only side left is the big diamond, so the big diamond is opposite the small square inside a square.

choice_feedback.A: The small diamond sits next to the small square inside a square, so it is not the side left over.
choice_feedback.B: The side with a line sits next to the small square inside a square, so it is not the side left over.
choice_feedback.D: The side with 4 boxes sits next to the small square inside a square, so it is not the side left over.
choice_feedback.E: The side with the X sits next to the small square inside a square, so it is not the side left over.
